standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that flatness propagates from M_1 to its cokernel along the induction step, makes the cokernel free over A once it is flat, turns the exact sequence into a universally exact one so that injectivity of the base changed map is detected on the presentation, and supplies the flattering criterion of the preceding theorem for the final corepresentation.

core_obligations: Reduce to a complete devissage: write B = C_q and M = N_q for a finite type ring map A -> C and a finite C-module N, note that F_lf is unchanged under replacing B by a local ring flat over it, and since A is henselian apply the existence lemma to assume a complete devissage of N over C over A at q (proof lines 6809-6821).

Reduce along the devissage: for a complete devissage (A_i, B_i, M_i, alpha_i, q_i) let q'_i be the unique prime of A_i over q_i, use the flat-at-a-point finite lemmas to pass from (M_1/A_1/A, q'_1) to (M_1/B_1/A, q_1), and then induct on the length n of the devissage, using that M_2 is the cokernel of alpha_2 to conclude the theorem for the cokernel of alpha_1 (proof lines 6823-6849).

Turn the reduction into a corepresentation: for A' in the category use the induction step to see F_lf is a subfunctor of the functor of the cokernel module, which is corepresented by A/J, replace A by A/J, use flatness of the cokernel together with the devissage to make it free over A, write the two exact sequences 0 -> N_1 -> M_1 -> Coker(alpha_1) -> 0 and B_1^{r_1} -> N_1 -> 0, observe that the first is universally exact so that injectivity of alpha tensor 1 is equivalent to the presentation map being an isomorphism, and conclude with the flatterling theorem that F_lf is corepresented by A/I (proof lines 6851-6891).

Prove finite generation of I in the finite presentation case: write I as the filtered union of its finitely generated subideals, use that F_lf is corepresented by A/I so that A/I is in the functor, and apply part (2) of the flat-at-a-point lemma to get A/I_lambda in the functor for some lambda, whence I = I_lambda (proof lines 6893-6901).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the henselian case with a complete devissage (proof lines 6809-6821).
Induct on the length of the devissage to reach the cokernel of the first step (proof lines 6823-6849).
Replace A by the corepresenting quotient of the subfunctor and identify F_lf with the functor corepresented by A/I through the universally exact sequence (proof lines 6851-6891).
Deduce finite generation of I from the filtered union argument (proof lines 6893-6901).
difficulty_reason: The theorem is the local flatterling statement: for a henselian local A, a B essentially of finite type over A and a finite B-module M, the functor of local homomorphisms along which the localisations of M are flat is corepresented by A/I for an ideal I, which is finitely generated when A -> B and M are of finite presentation (statement lines 6789-6807, tag 05PG). The counted proof is a genuine induction on the length of a complete devissage: it must transport corepresentability across the finite steps of the devissage, replace A by the quotient corepresenting the subfunctor coming from the cokernel, use that a flat such cokernel is free over A, and then recognise the remaining condition as the isomorphism condition for a presentation map via universal exactness before invoking the flatterling map theorem. The reduction chain is the substance, so the claim is H2.
